title: Click event
description: One click produced by the redirect. The redirect writes nothing to the database: it puts this payload in a bounded in-memory buffer, and the publisher sends batches to the attribution.ingest exchange. The worker inserts it per tenant under row-level security, idempotent on `event_id`, so a redelivered batch writes nothing twice. The payload carries no raw IP and no user agent string: device, browser, country and traffic class are already classified, and `visitor_hash` is the daily HMAC that a click and a page view can share only within one UTC day.

event_id.description: The event's identity, generated on the redirect path. The store is idempotent on it.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the host resolved to. The worker groups a batch by this and inserts each group in its own tenant-scoped transaction.

click_id.description: The click's identity. The signed token the redirect appends to the destination carries it, so a page view or a postback can name it.

destination_id.description: The destination the redirect chose, so a report can break clicks down by destination.

campaign_id.description: The campaign of the link, absent for a link outside a campaign.

occurred_at.description: When the redirect answered, in UTC. The day partition is chosen from it.

browser_family.description: A small closed list of families, never a version and never the raw user agent.

country.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country from the GeoIP database, absent when the reader is unavailable.

referrer_domain.description: The referrer's registrable domain only: no path, no query, no scheme.

entry.description: The `e` entry label the redirect received, such as `qr`, so a Tenant can compare a QR code with a link.

traffic_class.description: `BOT` is a crawler or a link-preview fetcher; `SUSPECT` is a visitor over the per-link click rate. A report excludes both by default, and neither is ever credited.

visitor_hash.description: The daily anonymous visitor hash: base64url of an HMAC over the tenant, address and user agent under a key that changes each UTC day, so a hash cannot be linked across days.
